I just finished Texhnolyze and am itching to discuss it with anyone who's seen it. There will be unmarked spoilers in this post and comments, so proceed with caution. I'll write a spoiler-free recommendation post later, so hang tight for that if you're dying to know what this show is about

BEWARE: Heavy spoilers beyond this point.

As I see it, the theme of this show can be boiled down to this: Humans have the innate drive to survive, but once they've have achieved immortality, or the ultimate form of survival, there is nothing left for them. Thus, the human drive to survive is paradoxical.

At the beginning of the show, we meet Ichise, a man who's lost everything and is simply trying to survive. He is an aimless, purposeless, and rash human being that strikes out at anything for seemingly no reason. He embodies the most basic human need: To survive. As the series progreses, Ichise gets texhnolyzed by the doctor, granting him an arm and a leg with which to preserve himself. However, his texhnolyzed limbs do not secure his basic needs, and thus do nothing to change him.

In this first part of the show, the main conflict is that of Yoshii, an interloper from above who has come to stir up the city of Lux. Despite his efforts, he is thwarted because, as Onishi puts it, Lux does not want a spectacle. In other words, Lux does not want the status quo upset. As things stand, people are surviving. They are not thriving, by any means, but they are able to live and some even hold hope of moving up in the world. The Raccan hopes to move up into the realm of the Organo and the Salvation Union. They, in turn, wish to live amongst the Class. As we later find out, the Class (or at least Kano) wishes to achieve evolution. In essence, when people believe that they can secure a better lot in the world, they are less apt to cause a ruckus. In the end, Yoshii is killed and Lux returns to normal.

In the second half of the show, Ichise is adopted into the Organo by Onishi. Once in the Organo, he begins to change. He is no longer a volatile and violent person because he no longer needs to focus on simply surviving. Now, he wants a purpose, and he finds a patchwork purpose in serving the Organo. This is the first example we see of people losing purpose once they no longer have to survive. When this happens, people beign to define themselves through others, such as how Ichise begins to act according to his place in the Organo.

We see this scenario acted out above the ground. As we find out, the people of the surface exiled all of the people who had "demons" inside of them to the underground city of Lux. The "demon" they mentioned is self-preservation. The people who had the pure drive to survive were confined to Lux. This accounts for the massive difference in behavior between the two places. In Lux, people are dirty, greedy, and vicious. They are the ones who will do what they must to survive, and they do. In contrast, the surface world is a docile and apathetic place. None of them have the will to survive, so they are left waiting to die. They have rid themselves of all the people who wish to kill them, and have nothing to fear. When one no longer has to focus on surviving, what is left? Everything becomes meaningless because you will live whether you do it or not. Thus, the people above ground have become ghosts who are barely human. This is why Yoshii comments on how much life energy Lux has.

The dilemma that presents itself is this: Once humans become secure in their survival, they become purposeless husks. But if they are focused only on surviving, they become depraved, and remain depraved until their needs are satisfied. People will always do bad things as long as it is in the interest of their preservation. So, what do we do? Kano's solution is to become more than human; to evolve. This is why he converted all of the people that flocked to him into Shapes. He drove humanity to insanity so that it would destroy itself, and his Shapes took root and began their evolution into the next form of human (symbolized by the projection of a flower that comes from Ichise's arm at the end of the show). But the Shapes are nearly unrecognizable as people. They look more like machines than they do living beings. So, what path do we take? Do we give in to our basic instincts and harm each other to survive? Do we secure our survival and doom ourselves to complacency? Or do we leave our humanity behind in order to achieve a chance at something more? This is the question that Texhnolyze asks.

@ShoGaNai Sorry for the slow response. I've been busy last couple of days. But oh well, here goes:

(Massive spoilers)

I think your analysis is good, but I disagree about the point. Not saying what you're seeing isn't there, but here goes my own thoughts. Sorry if they seen a bit jumbled, I don't remember details.

Texhnolyze is about nihilism and the meaningless of life, and it tells us to embrace that fact. It keeps showing us that life is meaningless and eventually it will all come to an end, and that said end is inevitable. It does so in a way without ever feeling heavy-handed or preachy. Either way, throughout the show, we get to see a lot of different people trying to find a purpose through their ideologies, but in the end, we see that it's all for naught. None of their ideologies manages to save anyone, nor does it manage to give them anything in the end.

It also shows how that, despite Class and Normal people are superficially living differently, they're still the same. Succumbed to human desires all the same, no matter, their status, rank, wealth or nobility.

It's also symbolic in how people follow the beliefs of Kanno/Saginuma and show those being reduced to something less than human symbolizing the nature of blindly following an ideology for personal gain and how it reduces your humanity. The results of their ideologies can be symbolic for the way people blindly following ideologies results in as well.

The surface world symbolizes the afterlife as well, showing the nature of a place where everything is happy - without sadness no happiness. It puts Lux (life) in a positive light to the surface world (the afterlife) thus saying that you shouldn't waste your life hoping to get rewarded for it when it's over.

The main characters in the show are representative, and they get killed off in a symbolic manner when what they represent die. For example, Shinji represents naivety and he gets killed off after him finding out the the class isn't... well, classy thus it breaks his idealism. Onishii represents order and he gets killed off when Lux succumbs into chaos. Ran represents future and gets killed off when the future of humanity is done. Doc represents science/progression and gets "killed off" when that gets thrown out of the window. Et cetera.

The Texhnolyziation is shown at the end as a non-issue, and that they're still human despite being Texhnolyzed. As Ichise says, "Hey I've changed, haven't I? Not because I got this arm. It's because I met you." While experiencing reality a bit different, he's still Ichise regardless, and what made him change wasn't the arm, it was people like Ran and Onishii.

People like Onishii was also Texhnolyzed, yet he was one of the most strong in will people in the show. What's also matters here is that people like Onishii and Shinji aren't blindly following ideologies despite it may seem so. They're following, with convictions their own beliefs. They're not restricted to an ideology, because they are the ideology. They don't stray from them, they stay through to their own beliefs with an iron will, and thus they are above simply following an ideology. they are free from the shackles that come with that. As Yoshii says:

"True freedom can't lean on anything. It is transient, lonely and arduous."

In opposition to Saginuma's:

"In reality, I am the sole embodiment of the people here."

All in all, Texhnolyze tells you that life is meaningless and it will all end eventually, and thus you shouldn't try to find meaning where there is none, and instead treasure and live life for what it actually is.
